titel: What if AI doesn’t speak your language?

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: How underrepresented languages are being brought into the age of artificial intelligence.
kurzfassung: Artificial intelligence tools are predominantly trained on English and other major languages, leaving thousands of mother tongues behind. Microsoft's Lingua project aims to collect data and build models for underrepresented languages in Africa, Europe, and Canada. Beyond language preservation, this technology enables local populations to access vital legal and agricultural information.
stichpunkte: Microsoft's Lingua project helps train AI models in underrepresented and indigenous languages.
The initiative addresses a potential AI digital divide for speakers of minority languages.
Projects in Malawi use AI models to provide pro bono legal information to women and children.
AI voice assistants like Sentai offer conversational support and daily check-ins for older adults living alone.
Guardian Labs developed an anti-fraud smartphone app to protect elderly users from phone scams.
Europe and the United States take fundamentally different approaches to technology regulation and market competition.
Nobi integrates fall detection and prevention technology into ceiling-mounted lighting fixtures.
Intuition Robotics designed an AI companion robot named ElliQ to reduce loneliness and isolation among older adults.

kapitel.titel: Regulating Tech in Europe and America
More Age-Tech: Smart Lights and Companion Robots

beschreibung:
English is the most widely-used language online. Internet material helps to train AI tools. So where does that leave people whose native language barely features on the web? We find out about a project helping AI to work in more of the world’s languages.
Also this week: regulating tech might sound about as appealing as a trip to the dentist. But, like your check-up, it is important. With Europe and the United States taking different approaches, we’ll ask who gets to set the rules, and what that means for the rest of us. And there’s a growing range of technology aimed at older people. We’ll look at some of the products out there, and ask how useful they really are.
Presenter: Shiona McCallum
Producer: Tom Quinn

untertitel: AI can only communicate in languages that it's been trained on.
